captions.Fig1: A six-record prefix is shared by two positive archives, I and II, corresponding to A and D in Supplement S1.6. Observed records are shaded; world labels and unread values are shown retrospectively and are unavailable to the acquisition policy. In I the unique minimum TRUE prefix leaves the candidate incomplete, whereas in II it leaves the right rival incomplete. Continuing from the common prefix, candidate-tail-first and right-tail-first routes have total costs (9,7) and (8,9). Mixing them with probabilities 16/23 and 7/23 balances their ratios at 25/23 on this pair. The global upper bound requires the full policy of Supplement S1.6; this two-world illustration alone is not a global optimality proof. The public domain permits independent [0,1]^2 completions; the displayed pair is not a two-world promise. All coordinates are exact, rows are disclosed in fixed order, prices are unit and setup is zero.
captions.Fig2: Analytically established acquisition regimes on diagonal bands. Each separate column represents one integer archive length N; no values between columns are implied. The completion width satisfies 0<d<=1. For K=3, the zero-overhead and first-supercritical regions include their upper boundaries and hold for arbitrary fixed positive row prices and nonnegative common setup. The marked five-row triangular case has unit-price, zero-setup ratios 71/67 and 15/14. For K>=3 at unit prices and zero setup, 0<dN<=1 gives the exact unbounded-domain formula; outside this range the general comparison provides bounds. At d=0 the positive class is empty and no acquisition ratio is assigned.
captions.Fig3: A fixed alphabet and the cost of requiring complete candidate observation. (A) The raw symbols are (0,0), (1,0) and (1,1). The displayed mean vectors of the two hard worlds use N=12 and q=3. Diamonds and squares mark candidates, coloured circles mark left rivals, and the shared right rival is (1,0); the two lines join the rivals. (B) Lower and upper bounds for accumulation points of the optimal acquisition ratios as integer N grows, on the continuous triangle with K=3, unit row prices and zero setup. The middle row restricts policies to full candidate observation before TRUE on every positive archive and has the exact asymptotic limit 12/11. The unrestricted randomised interval is [23/22,12/11], of width 1/22. These are analytic results, not confidence intervals or measured performance. Convergence and the exact asymptotic constants for unrestricted policies remain open.
